fixes.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives, baker. He tells Moses, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) Those men are dead, and that's the word Moses gets before he heads out. I think that's a good thing to hear before a trip like that.

Nobody in this passage promises to hide Moses, baker. The LORD's reason is simple: “…all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) He doesn't mention a hiding place or a plan to sneak around. The reason He gives is about those men.

The verse names a staff, not a horn, baker. It says Moses “…took the staff of God in his hand.” (Exodus 4:20) If he'd shown up with a horn, I bet he'd have announced himself to the whole road. The staff is what the text gives us.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, “…I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.” (Exodus 4:21) Moses is told to perform the wonders before Pharaoh, and the LORD tells him Pharaoh still won't let the people go. So no quick yes is coming, and Moses hears that before he even gets there.

“A holy nation” does show up later in Exodus (Exodus 19:6), friend, but not here. In this message to Pharaoh, the LORD says, “Israel is My firstborn son…” (Exodus 4:22) That's the line Moses is told to bring.

Zipporah, Moses' wife, is the one who steps in. She takes a flint knife, cuts off her son's foreskin and touches it to Moses' feet (Exodus 4:25). Then the text says, “So the LORD let him alone.” (Exodus 4:26) I think this is a heavy moment, baker.

Aaron, Moses' brother, isn't the one who steps in, friend. The text says Zipporah, Moses' wife, took the flint knife (Exodus 4:25). Aaron comes into the next verses, where the LORD had said to him, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” (Exodus 4:27) His part is the meeting, not the lodging place.

Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, isn't mentioned at the lodging place, baker. Moses said goodbye to him in verse 18, and the text says Moses took his wife and sons and headed back to Egypt (Exodus 4:20). The one who acts at the lodging place is Zipporah, Moses' wife, with a flint knife (Exodus 4:25).

The Nile isn't mentioned in this scene, friend. The LORD tells Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” and Aaron “…met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.” (Exodus 4:27) That's the place the text gives us.
Jethro's home isn't the meeting place the text gives, baker. It says Aaron “…met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.” (Exodus 4:27) The verse names the mountain of God, and that's the spot.

The text says Moses told Aaron everything, friend. “…Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.” (Exodus 4:28) So Aaron hears it all, signs included, and only after that do they assemble the elders (Exodus 4:29). Moses doesn't keep the signs to himself.

That's him, baker. “…Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses.” (Exodus 4:30) And Moses is the one who performed the signs before the people. Aaron brings the words, Moses brings the signs, and everybody has a job.

No sacrifices in this scene, friend. The text says, “And Moses performed the signs before the people…” (Exodus 4:30) The signs are what the LORD had commanded him to perform (Exodus 4:28). That's what the people see.

Songs aren't what the text names, baker. It says, “And Moses performed the signs before the people…” (Exodus 4:30) The word is signs, the ones the LORD had commanded him to perform (Exodus 4:28). I bet Moses is relieved nobody asked him to sing.

The text doesn't mention any request for more signs, friend. It says, “…and they believed.” (Exodus 4:31) The people hear the LORD's words, they see the signs, and then the text says they believed. That's where the verse lands.
